name: Mághdì
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Othaniel, Nlabephee Kefas. 2017. A phonological comparative study of the Jen language cluster. TCNN Jos MA thesis; also Norton & Othaniel 2020, Proc. 1st Adamawa Conf., 17-99.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record magh1238 (https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/magh1238) and English Wikipedia 'Maghdi language' (raw wikitext).
sources.note: Bibliographic only: 4 refs (Kleinewillinghöfer 1996; Norton & Othaniel 2020; Othaniel 2017; Ethnologue); Wikipedia stub cites Blench Atlas and Adelberger & Blench 2026 only.

sources.citation: Oppong Peprah, Miracle / AdaGram project (LLACAN). Burak language page; AdaGram publications and talks lists. https://llacan.cnrs.fr/AdaGram/
sources.note: No Maghdi page, publication or talk; Burak page states Kleinewillinghöfer 2015 and Norton & Othaniel 2020 'both provide short wordlists' and little else was known of the branch before 2022.

sources.citation: Adelberger, Jörg & Roger Blench. 2026. The peopling of the Muri Mountains, Northern Nigeria: evidence from linguistics and ethnography. Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online. doi:10.18716/OJS/AAEO/2026_12031.
sources.note: Nothing; sec. 3.4.1.5 p.26 gives identity only: Kode/Widala = Kholok [ktc] (Chadic) + Maghdi [gmd] 'or Tala' (Bikwin, Adamawa).

sources.citation: Norton, Russell & Nlabephee Othaniel. 2020. The Jen language cluster: a comparative analysis of wordlists. Language in Africa 1(3): 17-99. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-17-99.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent (0 hits). Maghdi [gmd] is one of ten varieties (Table 1 p.18); tone-marked 300-item wordlist in Appendix. Sec. 3.3 Tone pp.43-44: 'High, mid, low, falling and rising tones were noted... For now, we decline to reconstruct tone for items where tone is too inconsistent.'

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th ed. Entry 302 Maghdi.
sources.note: Nothing; entry lists names (Mághdì; Widala also applies to Kholok), location, <2,000 speakers (1992), classification 'Adamawa: Bikwin group', source Kleinewillinghöfer (1992); no linguistic references.

sources.citation: Norton, Russell. 2019. Comparative phonology of the Jen languages. Slides, 1st Adamawa Conference, Mainz, 9-11 Sept 2019.
sources.note: Wordlist/lexicostatistics tables with a Maghdi column; nothing on stress or tone rules.

sources.citation: Othaniel, Nlabephee Kefas. 2017. A phonological comparative study of the Jen language cluster. BA thesis (Glottolog lists as MA), Theological College of Northern Nigeria, Bukuru / University of Jos. 68 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.5 p.5 limits the study explicitly: 'this study aims a phonological comparison at the segment level'. Maghdi consonant/vowel inventory columns (sec. 4.1) and tone-marked cognate sets (sec. 4.2); no tone or stress section.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2011/2015. Bikwin-Jen Group. Adamawa Languages Project web page, JGU Mainz. https://www.blogs.uni-mainz.de/fb07-adamawa/adamawa-languages/bikwin-jen-group/
sources.note: Classification only ('Mak-Tala consists of two distinct languages: Maɣdi (Tala) and Mak'); nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 1995/2015 (ms.). Bikwin-Jen: comparative wordlist (Swadesh 100). Adamawa Languages Project, JGU Mainz.
sources.note: Tone-marked wordlist with a Maɣdi (Tala) column; no prose on prosody.
